title: Sponsor Eligibility File Cycles and Retroactive Roster Windows across the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
Four windows are scheduled per plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans: the calendar days between one sponsor eligibility file and the next, the calendar days the plan allows between a change happening at the sponsor and its appearance on that file, and the months back a sponsor may reach to add a retiree to its roster or to remove one from it.

| Group plan | Days between eligibility files | Days of file lag allowed | Months back an addition may reach | Months back a removal may reach |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Standard (PPO) | 30 | 45 | 3 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Enhanced (PPO) | 30 | 45 | 3 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Premium (PPO) | 14 | 30 | 6 | 3 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Standard (EGWP) | 30 | 45 | 3 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Enhanced (EGWP) | 30 | 45 | 3 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Premium (EGWP) | 14 | 30 | 6 | 3 |

## Points of judgement on the schedule

The first two windows are counted in calendar days and the last two in whole months; the four are not interchangeable with one another.

On every plan of the book the window for adding a retiree back reaches further into the past than the window for removing one: 3 months against 2 on the four plans on the 30-day file cycle, and 6 months against 3 on the two plans on the 14-day cycle.

The plans on the shorter file cycle are the plans on the shorter lag and the longer retroactive reach. A plan whose file arrives every 14 calendar days allows 30 calendar days of lag and reaches 6 months back for an addition; a plan whose file arrives every 30 calendar days allows 45 calendar days of lag and reaches 3 months back.
